title: Frenemies debuts on the H3 Podcast channel
summary: Ethan and Trisha Paytas launch a weekly co-hosted show blending H3 commentary with Trisha's unfiltered stories. It quickly becomes one of the most watched recurring formats in the H3 universe.

title: Episode 39 blow-up and Trisha walks off
summary: A heated argument over production pay, creative control, and past slights escalates on air. Trisha leaves mid-episode; fans clip the moment across Twitter and Reddit for weeks.

title: Ethan announces Frenemies is ending
summary: Two days after the walk-off, Ethan posts that the show will not continue. Both sides release competing narratives about money, boundaries, and mental health.

title: Merch and "blocked" drama resurfaces
summary: Trisha posts videos accusing the Kleins of unfair merch splits and feeling sidelined on Teddy Fresh promotions. Ethan responds with timeline receipts on H3.

title: Leftovers premieres with Hasan Piker
summary: H3 launches a politics-and-culture spinoff co-hosted with Hasan. The show targets a younger, very-online audience and becomes a staple for election-cycle commentary.

title: "Content Nuke" on Trisha and Moses
summary: Ethan publishes a long investigative-style episode compiling texts, clips, and third-party claims about Trisha and Moses Hacmon. The fandom splits between "accountability" and "pile-on."

title: H3 parodies James Charles "Hoodie" merch
summary: H3 sells a satirical hoodie riffing on James Charles's merchandise line. James responds on social media; the exchange fuels another cycle of beauty-community vs commentary-podcast discourse.

title: H3 deep-dives Vlog Squad injury allegations
summary: Following investigative reporting on a stunt-gone-wrong involving Jeff Wittek, H3 dedicates episodes to David Dobrik's team culture and sponsor fallout.

title: Second Circuit affirms H3 fair-use win vs Matt Hoss
summary: After years of litigation over a reaction video, the appeals court rules in favor of Ethan and Hila, affirming broad fair-use protection for commentary. The decision is cited across YouTube law explainers.

title: Triller sues H3 over Jake Paul vs Ben Askren stream talk
summary: Triller and Ryan Kavanaugh file a $50M defamation suit over H3 commentary about the Triller Fight Club broadcast. H3 frames it as SLAPP-style intimidation.

title: Judge dismisses Triller defamation case
summary: A federal judge throws out most claims against the Kleins, finding the challenged statements were opinion or non-actionable hype. Triller's remaining paths narrow sharply.

title: Keemstar vs H3 feud cycle peaks again
summary: Another round of #DramaAlert coverage and H3 response videos over creator misconduct allegations and platform politics. Neither side's audience expects a lasting truce.

title: Philip DeFranco and H3 trade public statements
summary: A segment about sponsorship ethics and "drama channel" incentives leads to dueling videos and Twitter threads. Fans map it onto broader "old YouTube vs podcast era" narratives.

title: H3 revisits James Charles allegation news cycles
summary: As new legal filings and platform suspensions hit the beauty space again, H3 devotes episodes to James Charles's history and sponsor exits — reigniting merch-parody callbacks.

title: Leftovers episodes stoke Ethan–Hasan tension on Gaza coverage
summary: Heavy news weeks strain the co-host dynamic: clip channels highlight disagreements on framing, guests, and when to platform opposing voices.

title: Clip war: Hasan reacts to H3 bits; H3 responds on air
summary: Twitch and YouTube cross-clips amplify perceived slights about money, politics, and "parasocial" audience management. Both fanbases trend opposing hashtags.

title: Public argument over charity streams and "performative" giving
summary: A Leftovers segment questioning creator-led fundraisers prompts Hasan to push back on stream. Trade blogs treat it as a proxy fight over who owns "online left" credibility.

title: H3 covers new Dobrik documentary and comeback press
summary: As David Dobrik mounts a partial return narrative, H3 revisits Vlog Squad accountability arcs and sponsor reinstatements — often with Leftovers political analogies.

title: 2025 feud milestone: dueling "statement" videos
summary: Both creators post long-form videos addressing the state of Leftovers, friendship, and ongoing Twitch/Youtube audience overlap. Comment sections become de facto timelines.
